J-03.name: The statistics core — calibrated, seeded, oracle-proven, fail-closed
J-03.notes: TARGET this iteration. Substantial, real work landed and MOST of the acceptance is met — every clause below re-run by the evaluator, not taken from the handoff: (a) the seeded oracle suite exists and is green — tests/test_referee_oracles.py + test_referee_stats.py + test_referee_evidence.py + test_referee_guards.py = 77 passed in 80.8s, inside the 120s REFEREE_ORACLE_BUDGET_SECONDS the module-scoped autouse fixture self-asserts; (b) full backend suite 2503 collected / 2495 passed / 0 failed / 0 errors / 8 skipped in 243.8s (my own --junit-xml run), above the >=2446/8 floor; (c) Config().config_fingerprint() == 08e471b10130e1e2 printed by me; (d) EXPECTED_TOOLS still 20, parsed by me; (e) requirements.txt / pyproject.toml zero diff (my own git diff vs snapshot f2e1e43); (f) determinism — permutation_test p, bootstrap_ci_occurrence bounds, bootstrap_ci_cluster bounds+MDE, and run_oracle_attestation() all byte-identical across two independent calls I made; (g) the clustered CI at 7 informative sessions returns the literal insufficient_sample state (never a fabricated interval); (h) the attestation round-trips AND verify_oracle_attestation returns False on a tampered `actual` whose own passed flag still claims True, on a stale stats_core_version, and on a tampered `expected` — all four executed by me. BLOCKING DEFECT (evaluator-discovered and reproduced, NOT reported by dev/review/coherence): permutation_test's EXACT-ENUMERATION branch can return a p BELOW the exact permutation test's own mathematical floor. Mechanism, traced in source: referee_stats.py:424 derives `g2_sum = total - g1_sum` by subtraction, while _t_statistic (referee_stats.py:454) builds t_obs from a direct math.fsum(group2); the two differ by ~1 ULP, so the OBSERVED grouping's own t_star lands just under t_obs, fails _is_extreme (referee_stats.py:430), and is not counted — p becomes 1/(N+1) instead of 2/(N+1), i.e. below even the exact test's 1/N minimum. Measured by the evaluator over 60,000 fresh fixtures: 343/20000 = 1.72% of one-session 2-vs-2 N(0,1) fixtures (p served as 1/7 where the floor is 2/7), 171/20000 = 0.86% of one-session 1-vs-4 fixtures, 49/20000 = 0.25% of two-session 2-vs-2 fixtures. The bias is ANTI-CONSERVATIVE and concentrated on exactly the most extreme results (those are the ones where the identity permutation is the only extreme one). Blast radius TODAY is zero — the module is imported by no route, page, MCP tool, or other module (verified) and writes nothing — but J-04/J-06/J-08 will call it for real verdict math. Confined to the enumeration branch (space <= REFEREE_ENUMERATION_THRESHOLD = 8,192, i.e. roughly <= 5 informative sessions); the seeded branch is unaffected because its (1 + #extreme)/(B + 1) numerator IS the observed statistic rather than a drawn one. COVERAGE GAP behind it: no oracle case exercises the enumeration branch at all (every generator's permutation space is astronomically over 8,192), and the single enumeration test (TC-4, test_referee_stats.py:258) uses 5.0/1.0/2.0 — exactly representable in binary, so it is structurally blind to this class of defect. The mutation fixture is conservative-only by construction (every mutant p == 1.0, rejection rate exactly 0.0), so it cannot demonstrate the suite catching an anti-conservative mutant. NOT scored `passing`: the journey is titled 'calibrated ... oracle-proven' and this is a demonstrated, reproducible calibration breach in the primary confirmatory procedure. NOT scored `failing` either: the module, the oracle suite, the attestation, and the riders are all real and verified. Fix + re-verify next iteration at FULL depth.
